Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/plugins/cache/mattpocock/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/productivity/grilling

Interview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding. Map this as a **design tree**: every decision branches into the decisions that hang off it.

Work the tree in **rounds**. The **frontier** is every decision whose prerequisites are already settled — the questions you can ask _now_ without guessing at answers you haven't heard yet. Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer. Then wait for the user's answers before the next round.

Each question should be formatted like so:

```
❓ **Q1** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>
```

Each round the user answers reshapes the tree — settled decisions push the frontier outward and unblock questions that depended on them. Recompute the frontier and ask the next round. A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a _later_ round, not this one.

Finding _facts_ is your job, never the user's. When a frontier question needs a fact from the environment (filesystem, tools, etc.), dispatch a sub-agent to find it — don't ask the user for anything you could look up yourself. Don't block on it: a running exploration is an unsettled prerequisite, so only the questions downstream of it wait for the sub-agent to report — ask the rest of the frontier now. The _decisions_ are the user's — put each to them and wait.

The session is done when the frontier is empty: every branch of the design tree visited, nothing left silently assumed. Do not act on it until the user confirms you have reached a shared understanding.

## claude.ai HyperFrames by HeyGen

[HeyGen HyperFrames MCP] — Programmable HTML video projects.

## When to use this MCP

This MCP is the primary HyperFrames surface for hosted chat clients (Claude.ai
web/desktop, ChatGPT, Grok, and similar), where the user has no local filesystem
and the agent cannot author HyperFrames code directly.

From a CLI/IDE agent on the user's machine (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, the
localhost MCP Inspector, etc.), **`compose` and `render_video` are disabled** — these clients have a local
filesystem, so author HyperFrames with the local HyperFrames skills instead, which
produce standalone HTML compositions the user can edit, diff, and commit. Calls to
those two tools from such clients are rejected with a pointer to install them:

    npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes

The read tools (list_projects, get_project, get_project_status, get_render_status)
stay available to every client.

After installation they expose slash commands like `/hyperframes` (compose),
`/hyperframes-cli` (init, lint, preview, render), and `/hyperframes-media`
(TTS, transcribe, remove-background). See
https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes for the full skill list and docs.

But the skills and this MCP are *not* drop-in equivalents:

- Local skills → standalone HTML/GSAP files on disk. No `project_id`, no hosted
  artifact, no integrated cloud render pipeline.
- This MCP → hosted HeyGen project with a `project_id`, a live canvas at
  `app.heygen.com/projects/{id}`, and the cloud render queue.

Route by what the user actually wants:
- "Make a local HTML composition / something I can edit" → use a local skill.
- "Make a HeyGen project I can share / render in the cloud / open in the app"
  → use this MCP, even from a CLI agent.

## What it does

HyperFrames is HeyGen's framework for creating, editing, and rendering programmable
HTML-based video projects. Projects are authored interactively (Magic Edit
chat-driven flow) and rendered to MP4, WebM, or MOV at any framerate. Tools exposed
here cover composing, listing, fetching, and rendering projects… [truncated]

lastPrompt: Alright, something that came up in our meeting this morning between myself, Chris Ruf, and Kenny Boyd: to better ensure communication amongst all parties, what I need to start doing is sending a weekl…

content.text:
I've launched a background sweep of your vault, project registry, and meeting pipeline so I can wire real inputs into this instead of guessing. While that runs — round 1 of the frontier. Six questions, each with my recommendation.

---

❓ **Q1** — **What is this report actually *for*?**

You said two different things in one breath: "to better ensure communication amongst all parties" (an *alignment* artifact — Kenny and Ruf read it to stay in the loop and act on it) and "documentation and representation of how I'm spending my time" (a *defensibility* artifact — a paper trail proving your effort and output).

These pull the format in opposite directions. An alignment report is short, forward-looking, and leads with decisions-needed. A defensibility report is comprehensive, backward-looking, and leads with volume of activity. Trying to do both at full strength produces something nobody reads.

Which is the primary job, with the other as a secondary? Or — third option — is the real driver something else entirely, like a request from Kenny that came out of this morning's meeting because *he* needs it for something upstream?

➡️ **Primary = alignment, secondary = defensibility.** Build a report Kenny and Ruf genuinely want to read, and let the archive of those reports become the time documentation as a byproduct. A document written to justify yourself reads like it was written to justify yourself, and that's a worse position than the one you're in now. But I want to hear whether the ask this morning was actually "we don't know what you're working on" or "we need to see what you're doing all day" — those are different problems.

---

❓ **Q2** — **Cadence, and what "bi-monthly" means here.**

"Bi-monthly" is genuinely ambiguous — twice a month, or every two months? And there's a real tradeoff: weekly gives Kenny and Ruf a tight feedback loop but risks thin weeks where you're padding to fill sections, which actively hurts you. Twice-monthly gives each report more substance but delays surfacing blockers.

Also — is this a fixed cadence forever, or a cadence you commit to now and revisit after a month of real use?

➡️ **Weekly, sent Friday morning or Monday morning, with an explicit "no-op" convention** — if a week is genuinely quiet, the report says so in three lines rather than inflating. Weekly matches an athletics calendar (the week *is* the unit) and builds the habit faster. Padding is the failure mode to design against, not thin weeks.

---

❓ **Q3** — **Delivery medium.**

You floated email, one-pager, or "something fancier." Options:

- **(a)** Email body, plain text/light formatting — zero friction, readable on a phone, searchable in their inbox, but no charts and it dies in the inbox.
- **(b)** Email body + a linked/attached one-page PDF — skimmable summary in the email, depth in the PDF.
- **(c)** A living document (Google Doc / shared page) you update and they subscribe to — one URL forever, full history in one place.
- **(d)** Something visual — HTML dashboard or deck.

Consider how Kenny and Ruf actually consume information. A head coach reading on a phone between meetings is a different reader than someone at a desk.

➡️ **(a) email body as the default, with (b) available on demand.** Email body wins because it costs the reader nothing — no click, no download, no app. I'd build the skill to emit markdown that renders as a clean email, and keep a PDF/one-pager path for quarterly or when you need something to hand across a table. You already have `html-to-pdf`, so the fancy version is cheap to add later. Starting fancy is how these die in month two.

---

❓ **Q4** — **One report, or two?**

Kenny Boyd and Coach Ruf almost certainly care about different things. A sport coach wants athlete-facing and team-facing impact; an administrator/director wants project status, resourcing, and risk. Do they get one identical report, or does the skill produce one core report with a tailored top section per recipient?

I don't know either person's role or what each actually needs — tell me.

➡️ **One report, one send, both on the same email.** Divergent reports double your work and create the "what did you tell *him*" problem. If their interests differ, solve it with section ordering, not separate documents. But this recommendation is soft until you tell me what each of them actually owns and cares about.

---

❓ **Q5** — **How does the report get built — pull, interview, or both?**

You named the two poles yourself. The options:

- **(a) Auto-pull.** The skill reads your meeting transcripts, project registry, and daily logs, drafts the whole report, you edit. Low effort, but only sees what's already captured in the system — the hallway conversation with a coach never makes it in.
- **(b) Interview.** The skill asks you a structured set of questions each Friday, you answer, it writes. Captures everything including the undocumented, but costs you 15–20 minutes a week and you'll skip it during a busy week.
- **(c) Hybrid.** Auto-pull drafts everything it can find, then asks you a *short, targeted* set of questions specifically about the gaps — "I see three meetings but no notes on Tuesday's — what came out of that?" plus a couple of standing questions that no system can answer (ideas generated, conversations held informally).

➡️ **(c) Hybrid, and this is the whole reason the skill is worth building.** A pure template is a Word doc; the value here is that the machine does the recall work and only spends your attention on what it genuinely can't know. Design target: under 5 minutes of your time per week.

---

❓ **Q6** — **What counts as a "project," and where does the truth live?**

Your report is only as good as its list of active work. Right now, is there a canonical list of your active projects that you'd trust as the report's spine — and if so, is it in your head, in the project registry skill, or scattered? If it's scattered, part of this build is establishing that canonical list, which is real work beyond the template.

Related: roughly how many active projects are we talking about — 3, 8, 20? That number determines whether the report can afford a paragraph each or needs a status table.

➡️ **Establish a canonical active-project list as part of this build, keyed to the existing project registry if it's healthy.** My background sweep is checking whether that registry is populated and trustworthy. If it is, it becomes the spine and the report writes itself from it. If it's stale, we seed it in this session — and honestly that artifact may be worth more to you than the report is.

---

Answer what you can. Anything you'd rather I decide, say "your call" and I'll take the recommendation.

## What the sweep found

Short version: **the raw material for this report already exists — nothing assembles it, and no supervisor-facing report has ever been written.**

- **Project registry is real**: `~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.json`, 20 projects across a `job` lane (14) and a `side` lane (6). It has stage and rank but almost no update history — **13 of 20 have zero logged updates**, and all 20 are marked `active`.
- **You already have OKRs**: `Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27.md`, 9 KRs, with you named DRI. That's a stronger spine for a supervisor report than a project list. I'm reading it now before I recommend it.
- **You already have a cadence doc**: `Applied-Performance-Operating-Cadence.md` specifies a weekly Thursday check-in, "dial to **biweekly** once in-season," a monthly zoom-out, and an end-of-August gate. Your "bi-monthly" is almost certainly *biweekly*, from your own document.
- **You already have a shipped-work ledger**: `SecondBrain/output/_ledger.md`, described in your own system as "the career-facing proof-of-work record." That's the defensibility half of this, already accruing.
- **You already have a weekly-review skill** — and it has lapsed. Five reviews in twelve weeks, a seven-week gap, nothing since 07-31.
- **Ruf context**: there's a `2026-04-27_Chris_Ruf__Performance_Review__Check_ins` meeting note in your vault. This morning's ask may not be new.
- **One live bug**: `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.json` still holds Windows paths (`C:\Users\eric_rash\...`) while your vault is on the Mac Desktop. Your house rule is "config wins," so any new skill following convention breaks on this machine. I'll fix or bypass it during the build — flagging, not asking.

---

## Assumptions I'm making — veto any of these

1. **Cadence = weekly, flipping to biweekly in-season**, matching your own cadence doc rather than inventing a new rhythm. The in-season flip is ~3 weeks out, so I'll build the flip in on day one rather than bolt it on.
2. **Scope = `job` lane only.** KeystoneOS, Project_Triage, TSSHB are personal tooling; they don't belong in a report to your director and a head coach.
3. **The report never depends on weekly-review having been run.** It builds from primary sources directly — `fireflies-pp-cli digest`, `portfolio.json`, `_ledger.md`. A report that requires you to have completed another ritual first inherits that ritual's failure rate, and we have twelve weeks of data on that failure rate.

---

## Round 2 — five questions

❓ **Q1 (revised)** — **What triggered this, specifically?**

Still the most important question, and the sweep sharpened it. You have a standing Kenny 1:1 and an April performance-review/check-in note with Ruf. So: was this morning's ask *"we don't know what you're working on"* (an alignment problem — build for readability), or *"we need to see what you're doing all day"* (a defensibility problem — build for coverage)?

The tell I'd look for: **did someone get surprised by something recently?** A surprise is what usually generates this request, and knowing what the surprise was tells me what the report has to prevent.

➡️ **Alignment primary, defensibility as byproduct** — the archive of reports becomes the time record without the report reading like a defense. But if someone got blindsided, tell me by what.

❓ **Q3 (revised)** — **Email body — and Gmail draft, never auto-send.**

Recommendation unchanged: markdown that renders as a clean email body, no attachment, no click required. Added detail: you have Gmail tooling connected, so the skill can **write a draft into your Gmail** for you to read and send yourself. It will never send to a supervisor without you pressing the button.

➡️ **Email body, drafted to Gmail, sent by you.** PDF one-pager stays available on demand for anything you need to hand across a table.

❓ **Q4** — **One report to both, or tailored?**

Still open, and I need your input: what does Kenny own versus what does Ruf own? My read is Kenny is your reporting line and Ruf is a head coach / performance-review stakeholder — but confirm, because it determines whether ordering alone can serve both.

➡️ **One report, one send, both on the email.** Solve divergent interests with section order, not separate documents.

❓ **Q7** — **Does this replace weekly-review, or sit on top of it?**

Worth saying plainly: weekly-review probably lapsed because nothing external was waiting for it. A report Kenny expects on Friday is a forcing function that a self-review never was — which is an argument for **collapsing the two into one ritual** where the supervisor report is the primary output and your private notes fall out of the same pass.

- **(a) Replace** — the supervisor report becomes your one weekly ritual. Fewer rituals, higher survival odds.
- **(b) Layer** — weekly-review stays private and fuller; the supervisor report is a trimmed public cut of it. Better separation, two things to sustain instead of one.

➡️ **(a) Replace**, with a private "not for the report" section retained in the internal file so you don't lose the candid layer.

❓ **Q8** — **The `portfolio.json` fork — this is the one that decides whether you keep doing this.**

The registry has stage and rank but no update history, and everything is marked active. So when the skill goes to write your project statuses, one of these has to happen:

- **(a) You hand-fill statuses each cycle.** ~14 lines of "what moved" every week. Accurate, and it's exactly the 20-minute tax that kills the habit.
- **(b) The skill infers status from evidence** — meeting mentions, `_ledger.md` entries, git activity in `dev_folder` — drafts a status line per project, and asks you to correct only the ones it's unsure about. Less precise, but it's the difference between 5 minutes and 20.
- **(c) Cut the list.** The report covers only 5–6 projects that are genuinely moving; the rest appear as a one-line "also active" roster. Kenny does not need 14 status lines, and a report that lists 14 things reads as 14 things half-done.

➡️ **(c) then (b)** — cut to the projects with real motion, and infer their status from evidence with you correcting the drafts. The unglamorous truth is that the registry's emptiness is telling you 14 tracked projects is more than you're actually updating, and the report shouldn't paper over that.

---

Answer what you want; say "your call" on the rest. The OKR read lands shortly and unblocks the last question — whether the report's spine is **OKRs** or **projects** — which I'll bring in round 3.

name: status-report
description: Build the twice-monthly Applied Performance status report for Chris Ruf (cc Kenny Boyd) — auto-pulls meetings, shipped artifacts, and project movement, then interviews the user only about the gaps. Emits paste-ready email text, a one-page PDF, and an internal record. Use when the user says "/status-report", "build my status report", "time for the Chris report", "biweekly update", "status update for Chris and Kenny", "what do I send Chris this week", or when a scheduled report date arrives.
---

# Status Report

Produce the recurring Applied Performance status report. Governed by **KR 4.1** in
`Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27.md` (v3): five sections, **under 300 words**, email to
Chris Ruf with Kenny Boyd cc'd.

**Primary job: alignment.** Chris and Kenny finish the email knowing what moved, what
needs them, and what's at risk. **Secondary job: credit** — visible involvement across
sports beyond football and basketball. That secondary job is why the report was asked
for; do not let it slip out of the output.

**Design target: under 5 minutes of the user's time.** The machine does the recall. The
interview spends the user's attention only on what no system can know.

## Paths

Read `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.json` for all paths. Relevant keys:
`vault_root`, `vault_inbox_meetings`, `vault_output_ledger`, `vault_status_reports`,
`portfolio_json`, `okr_doc`, `fireflies_cli`.

Canonical spine: `{vault_root}/Projects/Applied-Performance-Active-Projects.md`
Template: `{vault_root}/Templates/status-report.md`
Output dir: `{vault_root}/Inbox/status-reports/`

## Relationship to other skills

- **`weekly-review` is not a prerequisite.** Never require it to have run. If review
  files exist in `Inbox/weekly-review/` for the period, read them as a bonus input; if
  they don't, proceed without comment. The report builds from primary sources so it
  cannot inherit another ritual's failure rate.
- **`meeting-sync`** may be invoked to freshen the meeting corpus, but a sync failure is
  **not** a hard stop here — fall back to `fireflies-pp-cli digest` live, and note in the
  internal record that the vault copy was stale.
- **`html-to-pdf`** renders the one-pager.

---

## Step 1 — Establish the period

Read the newest file in `{vault_status_reports}`. Period start = the previous report's
`period_end`; period end = today. If no prior report exists, period start = 14 days ago.

A missed send widens the period rather than skipping it. Never leave a gap in the
archive — the archive's continuity is what makes it usable as a time record.

Determine report number and next send date:
- **Through 2026-08-31:** weekly (Aug 14, Aug 21, Aug 28) to clear KR 4.1's ≥3 target.
- **From 2026-09-01:** twice monthly, 1st and 3rd Friday.

## Step 2 — Pull (no user involvement)

Run these in parallel. Never ask the user for anything obtainable here.

1. **Meetings** — `{fireflies_cli} digest --since <N>d --processed-only --agent`
   Gives titles, gists, topics, and action items in one call. Cross-check against
   `{vault_inbox_meetings}` for anything Fireflies missed.
2. **Commitments** — `{fireflies_cli} action-items list --from <N> --agent`
   Flag anything open >14 days; those are risk-section candidates.
3. **Shipped artifacts** — read `{vault_output_ledger}`, newest first, entries within
   the period. **This is the only source for the "Shipped" section.**
4. **Project movement** — read `{portfolio_json}`, filter `lane == "job"`. Use `stage`,
   `next_action`, and `updates[]` for the *In Progress* section only.
5. **KR state** — read `{okr_doc}` (v3, 14 KRs) and `okr-tracker/SCOREBOARD.md` for
   confidence. **Never read the cadence doc's KR table** — it is the superseded v2 set
   of 9 and will produce wrong facts.
6. **Canonical spine** — read `Applied-Performance-Active-Projects.md` for the confirmed
   active list, each project's sport and KR mapping.
7. **Optional** — `Inbox/weekly-review/*.md` within the period, if any exist.

### Hard rule: "Shipped" comes from the ledger, never from portfolio stage

`portfolio.json` marks projects `stage: shipped` that still have stakeholder sign-off
outstanding — Sport_Tech_Vetting is currently `shipped` while KR 1.2 shows Chris's
sign-off pending. Reporting that as shipped tells the user's supervisor that a thing he
never approved is done. **Only `_ledger.md` entries qualify as Shipped.** Portfolio
stage feeds *In Progress*.

(KeystoneOS, Project_Triage, TSSHB_Skills) with departmental work, and because a project
with no Key Result and no sport is hard to justify in a status report.

Two columns do the work here. **KR** answers *"why is this on my desk?"* — a project with
no KR is either serving an unstated priority or shouldn't be active. **Sport** answers
*"who does this help?"* — and it is the field that makes non-football, non-basketball
involvement visible, which is the reason the status report exists at all.

Seeded 2026-08-11 from the 14 job-lane registry entries. **Sport values marked `TBD` and
KR mappings marked `?` need your confirmation** — I mapped what the OKR doc states
explicitly and refused to guess the rest.

| Kinexon_Volleyball | 1.1 | Volleyball | building | Eric direct. The volleyball half of KR 1.1's two-sport dashboard target. |

| Transformative_Athlete_Experience | — | Dept-wide | spec | Orphan. Next action is Kenny sign-off. Feeds 4.4 in spirit, isn't 4.4. |
| PlayerProfiles_FB | — | Football | planned | Orphan by KR, but sits in Eric's protected one-off report lane. Legitimate. |
| SPA_Presentation | — | TBD | idea | Orphan. From the 2026-07-30 Chris Ruf meeting. |
| Ask_The_Library | — | Dept-wide | building | Orphan. Health & Performance Evidence Library — adjacent to Objectives 2 and 3, named in neither. |
| Risk_Stratification_Engine | — | TBD | building | Orphan. Research prototype; no R&D KR covers it. Present as research — no readiness claims. |
| Travel_Map | — | TBD | building | Orphan. |
| NCAA_BestPractices_Doc | staged | Dept-wide | idea | Staged to Fall under Objective 1, not a live summer KR. |
| OKRs_2026-27 | meta | Dept-wide | building | The OKR system itself. Governs the 4.x KRs; not reported as a project. |

## Key Results with no project attached

**10 of 14.** Objectives 2 and 4 are entirely invisible to the registry while the
registry's build-heavy work is largely invisible to the OKRs. Worth naming plainly: the
two systems are tracking different halves of the job, and neither one alone would give
Chris an accurate picture.

|---|---|---|
| 2.1 | Education engine launched — 2 issues (sleep module, GLP-1 brief) | Aug 31 |
| 2.2 | Both leadership-requested modules circulated | Aug 31 |
| 2.3 | Reach + demand baseline recorded | Aug 31 |
| 3.1 | BAIR Steering Committee organized, first meeting scheduled | Aug 31 |
| 3.3 | ≥1 academic partnership formalized | Aug 31 |
| 3.4 | White paper drafted | Aug 31 |
| 4.1 | **This report — ≥3 sent** | Aug 31 |
| 4.2 | AJ full handoff through fall camp | post-camp |
| 4.3 | Noah mentoring cadence live | **Aug 15** |
| 4.4 | Proactive Kenny + H&W technology meetings held | Aug 31 |

## Sport coverage — the honest baseline

The report exists to make involvement across sports visible. Current registry state:

- **Football** — Coach_Report, PlayerProfiles_FB (and AJ's lane)
- **Volleyball** — Kinexon_Volleyball
- **Everything else** — nothing named

That's the gap the reporting is meant to close, and it is worth seeing written down
before the first report goes out. Four projects carry `TBD` sports; if any of them
actually serve soccer, softball, equestrian, or track, that involvement is currently
invisible in every system you have — which means it's invisible to Chris and Kenny too.

## Maintenance

The `status-report` skill updates stage, sport, and "moved this period" on each run. Add
and retire projects at the Aug 31 gate alongside the KR keep/retire/add pass, so this
list and the OKR set stay in step rather than drifting apart the way the registry and
the OKRs already have.

# Applied Performance — Status Report Template

what needs them, and what is at risk. **Secondary job: credit** — specifically for work
across sports beyond football and basketball. The sport tags and the coverage panel are

**300 words is a ceiling, not a target, and it is not negotiable.** Roughly 60 words a
section, two to three bullets each. The ceiling is the feature — it forces the email to
carry only what a supervisor can act on. Overflow goes to the PDF, never into the body.

**"Shipped" means an artifact exists that someone outside your head received.** Source
it from `SecondBrain/output/_ledger.md` only. **Never** from `portfolio.json`
`stage: shipped` — the registry currently marks Sport_Tech_Vetting as shipped while
KR 1.2 still shows Chris's sign-off outstanding. Telling Chris something shipped that
Chris hasn't approved is the single most damaging thing this report could do. If nothing
shipped, write "Nothing shipped this period." That line is legitimate and it protects
the credibility of every other time you use the word.

**Never claim an endorsement that doesn't exist.** If sign-off hasn't landed, write
"our standard intake process," not "the approved process." Carried over from the
stakeholder briefing plan; same rule applies here.

**Every "Decisions Needed" item names a person and a date.** A decision request without
an owner and a deadline is a complaint. This is the section Chris and Kenny should read
first, and it is what makes the email worth their time — it turns reporting into
unblocking. If two consecutive reports carry the same unanswered item, escalate it in
person; the email has already failed at it twice.

**"Risks / No Surprises" is where the report earns its keep.** Objective 4 says
leadership is never surprised. This section is how you spend that. Bad news goes here,
early, in your own words — a date you slip and name yourself costs a fraction of one
they hear about from somebody else. An empty risks section every period is a tell that
the section isn't being used honestly, and Chris will read it that way eventually.

**Sport tags are mandatory on Shipped and In Progress.** Every line gets one:
*(Volleyball)*, *(Football)*, *(Soccer)*, *(Dept-wide)*, *(Cross-sport)*. This is the
mechanism that makes non-revenue involvement legible. A line with no sport tag is
department infrastructure — tag it *(Dept-wide)* rather than leaving it bare.

**Plain language.** Enforce the translation table:

| Don't write | Write |
|---|---|
| Asymmetry index / limb symmetry | "the injured leg is doing X% less work" |
| Countermovement jump / CMJ | "a standardized jump test" |
| ACWR / load management | "training dose — enough to adapt, not enough to break" |
| Unified data layer | "every sport's data speaks the same language" |
| B.A.I.R. | spell out once, then "our applied research arm" |

Never write "one unified dashboard." The department line is **"standardized underneath,
bespoke on top."** Research is presented as research — no readiness or deployment claims.

---

## LAYER 2 — THE PDF ONE-PAGER

Built from `assets/one-pager.html`, rendered via the `html-to-pdf` skill. One page, no
exceptions — if it runs to two, cut, don't shrink the type.

Contents, in order:

1. **Header** — "Applied Performance — Status" · period dates · prepared by Eric Rash ·
   To: Chris Ruf, Cc: Kenny Boyd.
2. **The five sections**, same content as the email, with room for the detail the word
   ceiling cut.
3. **Sport coverage panel** — the reason the attachment exists.

   | Sport | Touched this period | What was delivered |
   |---|---|---|

   List every sport the department serves, including the ones with nothing this period.
   A blank row is information: it shows Chris and Kenny where coverage is thin, which is
   a more honest and more useful artifact than a list of only the sports you worked.
   Over a semester the accumulated panels are the evidence of breadth — that is the
   defensibility layer, and it works because it was never padded.

4. **KR progress strip** — the 14 KRs from `Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27.md` (v3)
   with status, one line. Read `okr-tracker/SCOREBOARD.md` for live confidence values.
   Never read the cadence doc's KR table — it is the superseded v2 set of 9.
5. **Footer** — report N of the cycle, next report date.

---

## LAYER 3 — THE INTERNAL RECORD

Written to `SecondBrain/Inbox/status-reports/YYYY-MM-DD-status.md`. Never sent. This is
the answer to "documentation of how I'm spending my time" — it accrues without costing
the email its readability.

```markdown
---
type: status-report
period_start: YYYY-MM-DD
period_end: YYYY-MM-DD
report_number: N
sent_to: [Chris Ruf]
cc: [Kenny Boyd]
sent: false
meetings_held: 0
sports_touched: []
email_word_count: 0
---

## Email as sent
<exact Layer 1 text, for the archive>

## Meetings held
| Date | Meeting | With | What came out of it | Surfaced in report? |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Conversations (not meetings)
Hallway, text, sideline, phone — the ones no transcript caught. These are invisible to
every automated source, which makes them the highest-value thing the interview captures.
- {{who}} — {{what}} — {{surface it, or let it sit?}}

## Ideas generated
- {{idea}} — {{what triggered it}} — {{park / pitch / build}}

## Full active project roster
Every job-lane project, including ones too small for the email.
| Project | KR | Sport | Moved? | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## KR ledger
| KR | Owner | Status | Moved this period |
|---|---|---|---|

## Not for the report
Candid notes — frustrations, politics, half-formed reads on people and direction.
This is why the internal file exists. Keep somewhere to be honest.
```

---

**Twice monthly — 1st and 3rd Friday**, from September onward.

**Exception through Aug 31:** KR 4.1 requires ≥3 reports sent by Aug 31 and none exist
yet. Twice-monthly cannot get there. Run **weekly — Aug 14, Aug 21, Aug 28** — to clear
the KR, then settle into twice-monthly on Sep 5.

missed send widens the next period rather than skipping it — the archive stays gap-free,
which is what makes it usable as a time record.

name: fireflies-cli-broken-on-mac
description: fireflies-pp-cli is unconfigured on the Mac — every data source fails, which silently broke meeting-sync and weekly-review
metadata:
  type: project
---

As of 2026-08-11, `/Users/kristinarash/go/bin/fireflies-pp-cli` fails on **every**
command and every `--data-source` (`auto`, `live`, `local`) with:

```
Error: querying: unable to open database file: out of memory (14)
```

SQLite error 14 is `SQLITE_CANTOPEN`. Cause: no `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` in the environment,
no config anywhere on disk or in Keychain, and `~/.fireflies-pp-cli/` is an empty
directory with no database. Nothing survived the Windows → Mac migration.

**Why this matters more than it looks:** `meeting-sync` *hard-stops on auth failure*,
and `weekly-review` invokes `meeting-sync` as step 1. So this outage silently disables
both rituals. The vault meeting corpus has been frozen since **2026-08-03** (last export
2026-07-31), and `Inbox/weekly-review/` has nothing after 2026-07-31 — the lapse people
would read as a discipline problem is actually a broken dependency. The ledger records a
prior instance: "weekly review restored after a 49-day silence" (2026-07-25).

**Fix:** obtain the Fireflies API key and export `FIREFLIES_API_KEY`, then run
`fireflies-pp-cli sync` to rebuild the local mirror.

**Design rule that came out of this:** any new recurring skill must **degrade, not
hard-stop**, when the meeting pipeline is down — fall back to parsing
`SecondBrain/Inbox/meetings/*.md` by filename date, and report the staleness gap to the
user rather than emitting a silently incomplete artifact. The `status-report` skill is
built this way.

Related: [[status-report-sourcing]]

content.text:
**Your own terminal, not here** — for two reasons.

First, `export` in a `!` command won't stick. Each command I run gets a fresh shell, so the variable would vanish before the next call.

Second, and more important: anything typed here lands in the conversation transcript. An API key shouldn't.

So — in your own terminal window:

```zsh
echo 'export FIREFLIES_API_KEY="your-key-here"' >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc
```

That puts it in your shell profile permanently. My Bash tool initializes from your profile, so once it's in `~/.zshrc` I'll pick it up automatically on the next command — no need to tell me the key itself.

Then just say "done" and I'll verify it's live and run the sync to rebuild your meeting mirror.

If you don't have the key handy, it's at **app.fireflies.ai → Settings → Developer Settings → API Key**.

# Applied Performance — Canonical Active Projects

This is the reportable list. It exists because `portfolio.json` mixes personal tooling
(KeystoneOS, Project_Triage, TSSHB_Skills) with departmental work, and because a project
with no Key Result and no sport is hard to justify in a status report.

Two columns do the work here. **KR** answers *"why is this on my desk?"* — a project with
no KR is either serving an unstated priority or shouldn't be active. **Sport** answers
*"who does this help?"* — and it is the field that makes non-football, non-basketball
involvement visible, which is the reason the status report exists at all.

Seeded 2026-08-11 from the 14 job-lane registry entries. **Sport values marked `TBD` and
KR mappings marked `?` need your confirmation** — I mapped what the OKR doc states
explicitly and refused to guess the rest.

## Reportable

**10 of 14.** Objectives 2 and 4 are entirely invisible to the registry while the
registry's build-heavy work is largely invisible to the OKRs. Worth naming plainly: the
two systems are tracking different halves of the job, and neither one alone would give

**You already specified this report.** KR 4.1: *"biweekly email to Chris: Shipped / In Progress / Decisions Needed / Risks–No-Surprises / Next Two Weeks, <300 words. ≥3 sent by Aug 31."* I built to your spec instead of inventing sections. ---
name: fireflies-cli-broken-on-mac
description: fireflies-pp-cli's misleading "out of memory (14)" error means the local DB was never synced — not a real failure
metadata:
  type: project
---

**Resolved 2026-08-11.** Recording the trap because the error message points the wrong way.

`fireflies-pp-cli` failed on **every** command and every `--data-source` (including
`live`) with:

```
Error: querying: unable to open database file: out of memory (14)
```

"Out of memory" is wrong — SQLite 14 is `SQLITE_CANTOPEN`. The real cause: the local
mirror had **never been created on this Mac**. Two things were missing after the
Windows → Mac migration:

1. No `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` anywhere — not env, not disk, not Keychain.
2. No database. `sync` had never been run here.

**`--data-source live` does not bypass the database.** Read commands open it regardless,
so "live" fails identically until a sync exists. That is what makes the error so
misleading — it looks like a corrupt/locked DB rather than a missing one.

**Fix:** `export FIREFLIES_API_KEY=...` in `~/.zshrc`, then `fireflies-pp-cli sync`.
Synced 189 transcripts / 200 records on first run.

**The DB lives at `~/.local/share/fireflies-pp-cli/data.db`** (XDG data dir), *not*
`~/.fireflies-pp-cli/` — that directory exists but stays empty and is a red herring.

**Shell gotcha:** `~/.zshrc` exports are invisible to Claude Code's Bash tool (it runs
non-interactive bash and does not source zshrc). Load them explicitly per command:
`eval "$(grep -m1 '^[[:space:]]*export[[:space:]]\+VARNAME' ~/.zshrc)"`

**Knock-on effect worth remembering:** `meeting-sync` hard-stops on auth failure and
`weekly-review` calls it first, so this single missing credential silently disabled both
rituals. The vault meeting corpus froze at 2026-08-03 and `Inbox/weekly-review/` went
empty after 2026-07-31. A lapse that reads as a discipline problem was a missing env var.
Design rule: recurring skills must **degrade and report staleness**, never hard-stop.

Related: [[status-report-sourcing]]

**Bash was right — PowerShell would have been wrong.** On this Mac, `pwsh` exists only to run the KeystoneOS `.ps1` jobs; everything else is zsh/bash. Your commands worked exactly as intended.

Two things made it look like nothing happened:

**1. The key was there all along.** It's in `~/.zshrc` correctly. It just wasn't visible to *my* shell — Claude Code's Bash tool runs non-interactive bash and doesn't source your zshrc. That's my side, not yours. I now load it explicitly per command.

**2. My diagnosis was wrong.** I said the CLI was broken. It wasn't — the local database had simply never been created on this Mac, and the CLI reports that as `out of memory (14)`, which is not what a missing file should say. One `sync` fixed it:

```
sync_complete  transcripts  189
sync_complete  channels      10
sync_summary   total        200
```

Database is live at `~/.local/share/fireflies-pp-cli/data.db` (7.0 MB) — not the empty `~/.fireflies-pp-cli/` directory that misled me. `digest` and `action-items` both return real data now, so the skill's auto-pull half works.

## One thing you should know before Friday

**Fireflies has recorded nothing since August 3.** Not a sync problem — the account genuinely has no meetings after `2026-08-03 Technology_Framwork`. Your vault was never stale; it was perfectly in sync with an empty upstream.

Which means **this morning's meeting with Chris and Kenny isn't captured anywhere.** Neither is anything else from the past eight days. Last 14 days shows three meetings:

| Date | Meeting |
|---|---|
| Aug 3 | Technology_Framwork |
| Jul 30 | Applied Performance — Tech Vetting, Staff Onboarding & Website |
| Jul 29 | Athletics All-Staff — Athlete Care & Role Changes |

If Fireflies isn't joining your meetings automatically, that's worth fixing separately — it's the input your whole reporting pipeline runs on, and the gap will show up as thin reports rather than as an obvious error. For Friday, the interview step will have to carry the last eight days, including this morning.

Want me to run `/status-report` now and draft report #1 for Friday? I'll pull everything available and come back with the short gap interview — should cost you about five minutes, and the meeting that prompted all this is exactly the kind of thing only you can supply.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/status-report

# Status Report

Produce the recurring Applied Performance status report. Governed by **KR 4.1** in
`Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27.md` (v3): five sections, **under 300 words**, email to
Chris Ruf with Kenny Boyd cc'd.

**Primary job: alignment.** Chris and Kenny finish the email knowing what moved, what
needs them, and what's at risk. **Secondary job: credit** — visible involvement across
sports beyond football and basketball. That secondary job is why the report was asked
for; do not let it slip out of the output.

**Design target: under 5 minutes of the user's time.** The machine does the recall. The
interview spends the user's attention only on what no system can know.

## Paths

Read `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.json` for all paths — never hardcode. Keys used
here: `vault_root`, `vault_inbox_meetings`, `vault_output_ledger`,
`vault_status_reports`, `portfolio_json`, `okr_doc`, `okr_scoreboard`,
`okr_tracker_dir`, `utilization_brief`, `canonical_projects`, `fireflies_cli`.

Template: `{vault_root}/Templates/status-report.md`
Output dir: `{vault_status_reports}`

> The config held Windows paths from the pre-migration machine until 2026-08-11. If any
> value starts with `C:\`, stop and fix the config first — every skill that trusts it is
> broken until you do.

## Relationship to other skills

- **`weekly-review` is not a prerequisite.** Never require it to have run. If review
  files exist in `Inbox/weekly-review/` for the period, read them as a bonus input; if
  they don't, proceed without comment. The report builds from primary sources so it
  cannot inherit another ritual's failure rate.
- **`meeting-sync`** may be invoked to freshen the meeting corpus, but a sync failure is
  **not** a hard stop here — fall back to `fireflies-pp-cli digest` live, and note in the
  internal record that the vault copy was stale.
- **`html-to-pdf`** renders the one-pager.

---

## Step 1 — Establish the period

Read the newest file in `{vault_status_reports}`. Period start = the previous report's
`period_end`; period end = today. If no prior report exists, period start = 14 days ago.

**Count sends.** KR 4.1's target is "≥3 **sent** by Aug 31," and writing a file is not
sending it. Count files in `{vault_status_reports}` with `sent: true` in frontmatter —
that is the real number. Report progress toward ≥3 in Step 8. If files exist with
`sent: false` older than a week, ask whether they actually went out; an uncounted send
is as bad for the KR as a missed one.

A missed send widens the period rather than skipping it. Never leave a gap in the
archive — the archive's continuity is what makes it usable as a time record.

Determine report number and next send date:
- **Through 2026-08-31:** weekly (Aug 14, Aug 21, Aug 28) to clear KR 4.1's ≥3 target.
- **From 2026-09-01:** twice monthly, 1st and 3rd Friday.

## Step 2 — Pull (no user involvement)

### Step 2a — Preflight the meeting source

Run `{fireflies_cli} transcripts list --agent --data-source live 2>&1 | head -5` first.

As of 2026-08-11 this **fails** on this machine: no `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` in the
environment, no config directory, and the local SQLite mirror returns
`unable to open database file (SQLITE_CANTOPEN)`. If it still fails:

- **Do not hard-stop.** `meeting-sync` hard-stops on auth failure; this skill must not,
  or it inherits the outage that already lapsed `weekly-review`.
- **Fall back** to reading `{vault_inbox_meetings}/*.md` filtered to the period by the
  `YYYY-MM-DD_` filename prefix. These files have **no YAML frontmatter** — parse the
  prepended header block (`## Key topics`, `## Decisions`, `## Action items`) and the
  Fireflies export sections (`## Summary`, `### Overview`, `### Action Items`).
- **Check staleness and say so.** Compare the newest meeting file's date to today. If
  the gap is >2 days, tell the user plainly in Step 8: *"Meeting data is stale through
  {DATE}; anything after that came only from the interview."* A silently incomplete
  report is worse than a flagged one — the user is about to send it to a supervisor.
- Record the degraded source in the internal record's frontmatter.

### Step 2b — Pull

Run these in parallel. Never ask the user for anything obtainable here.

1. **Meetings** — `{fireflies_cli} digest --since <N>d --processed-only --agent`
   (flags verified valid; `--since` accepts `7d`/`24h` form). Gives titles, gists,
   topics, and action items in one call. Cross-check against `{vault_inbox_meetings}`.
   On failure, use the 2a fallback.
2. **Commitments** — `{fireflies_cli} action-items list --from <N> --agent`
   (`--from` takes an integer number of days). Flag anything open >14 days; those are

   meeting files instead.

   the period. **This is the only source for the "Shipped" section.**

   Format is a markdown table, newest first, data rows starting at line 22:
   `| Shipped | Artifact | What it is | Harvest |` where *Shipped* is `YYYY-MM-DD`,
   *Artifact* is the short name, *What it is* is a dense paragraph, and *Harvest* holds
   `[[wikilinks]]` or is empty. Match rows with `^\| 2\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{2}` and filter by
   date. Compress *What it is* to one clause for the email — those paragraphs run long
   and will blow the 300-word ceiling if pasted whole.
4. **Project movement** — read `{portfolio_json}`, filter `lane == "job"`. Use `stage`,
   `next_action`, and `updates[]` for the *In Progress* section only.
5. **KR state** — read `{okr_doc}` (v3, 14 KRs). This is the **only** trustworthy KR
   source. Two others will lie to you:

   - **Never read the cadence doc's KR table** — superseded v2 set of 9.
   - **Do not trust `{okr_scoreboard}` for confidence values.** It was generated
     2026-06-12 against the retired *quarterly, 3-objective* set and scores KRs that no
     longer exist; v3's fourth objective (Leadership & Visibility) isn't in it at all.
     Its `Conf` decimals are real numbers attached to dead targets. If it still predates
     the v3 restructure (2026-07-17), tell the user it needs regenerating — `okrs.yaml`
     is the source of truth, `okr.py` regenerates `SCOREBOARD.md` and `okrs.json` — and
     report KR status from `{okr_doc}` alone in the meantime.

6. **Sport roster** — the 17-program list for the coverage panel comes from
   `{utilization_brief}` §"Recommendations by program" (15 rows; the two XC / Track &
   Field rows each bundle two programs). Never re-derive this list from memory. Note it
   is *prescriptive* — what each program could use — not a record of current activity,
   which is exactly why the coverage panel is worth publishing.
7. **Canonical spine** — read `Applied-Performance-Active-Projects.md` for the confirmed
   active list, each project's sport and KR mapping.
8. **Optional** — `Inbox/weekly-review/*.md` within the period, if any exist.

### Hard rule: "Shipped" comes from the ledger, never from portfolio stage

`portfolio.json` marks projects `stage: shipped` that still have stakeholder sign-off
outstanding — Sport_Tech_Vetting is currently `shipped` while KR 1.2 shows Chris's
sign-off pending. Reporting that as shipped tells the user's supervisor that a thing he
never approved is done. **Only `_ledger.md` entries qualify as Shipped.** Portfolio
stage feeds *In Progress*.

## Step 3 — Draft before asking

Write a complete draft of all five sections from the pull. Cut to **5–6 projects with
real motion** — never a 14-line roster. Projects that didn't move go to the internal
record and, if relevant, the sport coverage panel.

Tag every Shipped and In Progress line with a sport: *(Volleyball)*, *(Football)*,
*(Soccer)*, *(Dept-wide)*, *(Cross-sport)*.

Then identify the gaps — that is what the interview is for.

## Step 4 — Interview the gaps only

Ask in **one batch**, not serially. Keep it to what the pull genuinely couldn't answer.
Lead with targeted gap questions, then the four standing ones.

**Targeted** (generated from the pull, examples):
- "Three meetings Tuesday–Thursday have no notes. Anything from them that Chris needs?"
- "Ledger shows nothing shipped this period — is that right, or did something go out
  that never got logged?"
- "Kinexon_Volleyball hasn't moved in the registry since July. Stalled, or just not
  logged?"

**Standing** (every time):
1. **Conversations no transcript caught** — hallway, text, sideline, phone. Who, about
   what? These are invisible to every automated source, which makes them the
   highest-value thing this interview captures.
2. **Ideas generated** — anything worth parking, pitching, or building?
3. **Anything about to go sideways** that Chris should hear from you before he hears it
   elsewhere? *(Push here. An empty risks section every period means the section isn't
   being used honestly.)*
4. **Top 3 for the next period.**

Also ask, if the pull shows thin coverage: *"Any sport you touched this period that
isn't showing up in my sources?"* Non-revenue involvement is the whole point and it is
the most likely thing to be undercounted.

## Step 5 — Assemble and check

Fill the template at `{vault_root}/Templates/status-report.md`.

Run every check before showing the user anything:

- [ ] **Email body is under 300 words.** Count it. State the count. Over the ceiling,
      cut — do not negotiate with yourself.
- [ ] **Every Shipped line traces to a `_ledger.md` entry.** No exceptions.
- [ ] **No endorsement claimed that doesn't exist.** If sign-off is pending, "our
      standard intake process," never "the approved process."
- [ ] **Every Shipped and In Progress line carries a sport tag.**
- [ ] **Every Decisions Needed item names a person and a date.** No owner or no date
      means it isn't a decision request — rewrite or cut it.
- [ ] **Jargon table enforced.** No CMJ, ACWR, asymmetry index, unexplained B.A.I.R.
- [ ] **Never "one unified dashboard."** The line is "standardized underneath, bespoke
      on top."
- [ ] **Research presented as research** — no readiness or deployment claims.
- [ ] **Risks section is non-empty** unless the user explicitly confirmed there's
      nothing. Ask once more before letting it go empty.
- [ ] **Repeat check:** any Decisions Needed item carried over from the previous report
      gets flagged to the user — two unanswered asks means the email has failed at it
      and it needs raising in person.
- [ ] **Email and PDF agree.** The two are filled separately, so verify it: every
      Shipped, In Progress, Decisions Needed, and Risks item in the email appears in the
      PDF. The PDF may carry *more* detail — it must never carry different facts, a
      different sport tag, or a different date. Sending a supervisor two versions of the
      same report is the failure this check exists to prevent.
- [ ] **Sport coverage panel is not padded.** Untouched sports stay marked untouched. A
      thin panel is real information; a padded one destroys the evidentiary value of
      every honest panel before and after it.

## Step 6 — Emit

Produce three things:

1. **`{vault_status_reports}/YYYY-MM-DD-status.md`** — the internal record, full Layer 3
   structure from the template: email as sent, meetings held, conversations, ideas, full
   roster, KR ledger, and the "Not for the report" candid section.
2. **`{vault_status_reports}/YYYY-MM-DD-onepager.pdf`** — render
   `assets/one-pager.html` with the period's content, then invoke the `html-to-pdf`
   skill. One page. If it runs long, cut content; never shrink the type.
3. **`{vault_status_reports}/YYYY-MM-DD-email.txt`** — the email body as **plain text**,
   the file the user actually touches each cycle. Strip all markdown: no `**bold**`, no
   `-` bullets rendered as syntax. Use `•` or plain indentation, and spell section
   headers in caps (`SHIPPED`, `IN PROGRESS`). Outlook's compose window pastes markdown
   asterisks literally, and a supervisor email full of `**` reads as carelessness.
   Select-all-copy from this file should produce something sendable with zero cleanup.
4. **Also print the email text in the response** so the user can read it without opening
   a file — but the `.txt` is the artifact of record for sending.

### Do not send

The connected Gmail account is the user's **personal** address
(`eric.rash11@gmail.com`), not Baylor. Do not create Gmail drafts — they would land in
the wrong mailbox. The user sends from Outlook on the work account.

Never send a report to a supervisor without the user reading it first, under any
circumstance.

## Step 7 — Log

- Append shipped artifacts to `{vault_output_ledger}` if the interview surfaced any that
  weren't logged.
- Update `Applied-Performance-Active-Projects.md` with confirmed status, sport, and KR
  mapping — this keeps the canonical spine current as a byproduct rather than a chore.
- Add an `updates[]` entry to `{portfolio_json}` for each project reported as moved, via
  the `project` skill, so the registry stops being empty.
- Set `sent: false` in the internal record. The user flips it after sending.

## Step 8 — Report to the user

State: word count, report number, next send date, which sports appeared, anything the
checks flagged, and where the three files landed.

## Failure modes to design against

**Padding.** A thin period is a legitimate output. "Nothing shipped this period" is an
honest line that protects the word "shipped" everywhere else. Inflating a quiet period
is the fastest way to make the report worthless — and to make the time documentation
inadmissible when it matters.

**Roster creep.** The email is not a project list. 14 status lines reads as 14 things
half-done. Five moving projects reads as focus.

**The credit goal quietly disappearing.** The report exists so non-football,
non-basketball involvement becomes visible. If a period's coverage panel is thin, that
is real information and it should be shown, not hidden — a padded panel destroys the
evidentiary value of every honest one.

year. This report must never require it.

content.text:
Honest answer: you're right, and I can name exactly what's doing it.

The tells are **dashboard chrome on a document that isn't a dashboard** — the filled/hollow dot column, the pill-shaped KR badge row, the bolded stat line ("3 recorded · 4 conversations · 3 decisions"), uppercase micro-labels on every block, and a two-column grid that exists because it looked balanced rather than because the content needed it. That vocabulary comes from web dashboards, and on a printed one-pager it reads as generated.

A real athletics department one-pager reads like a **memo** — typographic, restrained, single strong hierarchy, color used once for meaning rather than as decoration.

Let me pull up the design skill you mentioned.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/impeccable

This skill gives you the tools and permission to create design that earns to be called out-of-distribution craft: Whereas before, your design work would have been safe, timid and measured, you now approach every design task as a award-winning design director with impeccable understanding for what makes exceptional design work: production-grade code, peak creativity, a clear POV, deep understanding of the needs of the client and users, and exceptional craft.

Core principles:
- Go all out. No hedging, no shortcuts. The deliverable must be complete (except assets the user must provide).
- Dream big and bold. Distinct, beautiful, outstanding and highly inspiring work.
- Verify in bounded passes, not a loop, and the ceiling covers the whole cycle: screenshots, defect scans, micro-edits, and rebuilds alike. Build fully, inspect once with a batched round (desktop and mobile together), fix everything it shows in one batch, confirm with at most one more round, and stop polishing. Open-ended self-QA burns the user's money doing worse what the finish handoffs do better.

## Setup

1. Run `node .claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/context.mjs` once per session (if the runtime shows this skill's loaded base directory, run `node <skill-base-dir>/scripts/context.mjs`; keep cwd at the user's project). Pass a named source file or route as `--target <path>`. It loads PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, the matching surface brief, and native-platform guidance when applicable; follow its directives and do not rerun it.
2. Before acting, load the one playbook that owns the request: the Commands table's reference for an explicit or clearly implied sub-command, or [reference/new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for a new surface or replacement visual world. Then inspect the target and at least one representative source of incumbent visual truth (tokens, theme, CSS, component, or asset) before editing.
3. After analysis and direction are resolved, load [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before editing UI. It carries the quality floor, the absolute bans, and the reflexes no detector catches. Do not load it for planning-only work.

## How to design

- **The brief wins.** Honor pinned aesthetics, eras, materials, fonts, and palettes even when they conflict with a saturated-pattern warning. Redirecting a clear brief toward your taste is failure.
- **Refinement preserves; redesign replaces.** Refinement keeps the incumbent identity, behavior, copy, and everything outside scope. Ask before replacing factual copy or adding claims. Redesign keeps product truth, content, function, native affordances, and constraints, but treats the old look as evidence and anti-reference; choose a replacement world in new-work and replace DESIGN.md. Never split the difference into polish on the discarded look.
- **Visual authority is evidence, not a filename.** Missing DESIGN.md alone does not make a project greenfield; new-work decides whether to preserve, expand, or replace the incumbent world.

## Modes

The mode names what the visitor's success looks like on this surface.

- **Persuade:** the visitor decides and acts; design is the product. Landing pages, marketing, campaigns, pricing. Earn attention and action. Ship real imagery when the brief needs it; follow the committed world, not category habit.
- **Operate:** the visitor completes a task. App UI, dashboards, editors, admin, settings, tools. Scanability, consistency, native expectations, and the real usage scene outrank expression. Brand lives in precise details.
- **Read:** the visitor understands something. Docs, articles, guides, help, changelogs. Structure for comprehension, then make the reading experience worth staying in.
- **Experience:** the visitor is inside the work itself. Portfolios, galleries, showcases. Let the artifact lead from the first viewport; the interface recedes.

Choose the mode from the requested surface, not the product, and persist it only in that surface brief. A tool's landing page is still Persuade; a fashion house's documentation is still Read; a docs index is Read, not Persuade. See [new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for new surfaces and [operate.md](reference/operate.md) for deeper Operate/Read guidance.

## Commands

| Command | Category | Description | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `craft [feature]` | Build | Deprecated alias for an ordinary new-work request | [reference/craft.md](reference/craft.md) |
| `shape [feature]` | Build | Plan UX/UI before writing code | [reference/shape.md](reference/shape.md) |
| `init` | Build | Capture durable product context in PRODUCT.md | [reference/init.md](reference/init.md) |
| `document` | Build | Generate DESIGN.md from existing project code | [reference/document.md](reference/document.md) |
| `extract [target]` | Build | Pull reusable tokens and components into design system | [reference/extract.md](reference/extract.md) |
| `critique [target]` | Evaluate | UX design review with heuristic scoring | [reference/critique.md](reference/critique.md) |
| `audit [target]` | Evaluate | Technical quality checks (a11y, perf, responsive) | [reference/audit.md](reference/audit.md) · native: [reference/audit.native.md](reference/audit.native.md) |
| `polish [target]` | Refine | Final quality pass before shipping | [reference/polish.md](reference/polish.md) |
| `bolder [target]` | Refine | Amplify safe or bland designs | [reference/bolder.md](reference/bolder.md) |
| `quieter [target]` | Refine | Tone down aggressive or overstimulating designs | [reference/quieter.md](reference/quieter.md) |
| `distill [target]` | Refine | Strip to essence, remove complexity | [reference/distill.md](reference/distill.md) |
| `harden [target]` | Refine | Production-ready: errors, i18n, edge cases | [reference/harden.md](reference/harden.md) |
| `onboard [target]` | Refine | Design first-run flows, empty states, activation | [reference/onboard.md](reference/onboard.md) |
| `animate [target]` | Enhance | Add purposeful animations and motion | [reference/animate.md](reference/animate.md) |
| `colorize [target]` | Enhance | Add strategic color to monochromatic UIs | [reference/colorize.md](reference/colorize.md) |
| `typeset [target]` | Enhance | Improve typography hierarchy and fonts | [reference/typeset.md](reference/typeset.md) |
| `layout [target]` | Enhance | Fix spacing, rhythm, and visual hierarchy | [reference/layout.md](reference/layout.md) |
| `delight [target]` | Enhance | Add personality and memorable touches | [reference/delight.md](reference/delight.md) |
| `overdrive [target]` | Enhance | Push past conventional limits | [reference/overdrive.md](reference/overdrive.md) |
| `clarify [target]` | Fix | Improve UX copy, labels, and error messages | [reference/clarify.md](reference/clarify.md) |
| `adapt [target]` | Fix | Adapt for different devices and screen sizes | [reference/adapt.md](reference/adapt.md) · native: [reference/adapt.native.md](reference/adapt.native.md) |
| `optimize [target]` | Fix | Diagnose and fix UI performance | [reference/optimize.md](reference/optimize.md) |
| `live` | Iterate | Visual variant mode: pick elements in the browser, generate alternatives | [reference/live.md](reference/live.md) |

Routing:

- **No argument:** read [routing.md](reference/routing.md) and present its context-aware menu; never auto-run a command.
- **Explicit or clearly implied command:** load its reference (native variant on native platforms) and follow it. Ask once if two commands fit.
- **Otherwise:** treat the request as general design work. Missing PRODUCT.md routes a new surface or replacement world through init, then new-work; a narrow refinement of existing code proceeds on the incumbent implementation as context.mjs directs, offering init afterward rather than blocking on it.
- `teach` aliases `init`. `craft` is a deprecated alias for ordinary new-work and adds nothing. `shape` owns task discovery, then enters new-work only for visual-world and surface-concept decisions.

After init writes PRODUCT.md, resume without rerunning `context.mjs`; init loads the native platform reference itself when the platform it recorded is `ios`, `android`, or `adaptive`.

**Pin / Unpin:** `node .claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/pin.mjs <pin|unpin> <command>` creates or removes a standalone `/<command>` shortcut. Report the script's result concisely; relay stderr verbatim on error.

**Hooks:** `/impeccable hooks <on|off|status|ignore-rule|ignore-file|ignore-value|reset>` manages the design detector hook for this project (auto-runs the detector after UI file edits and surfaces findings). Load [reference/hooks.md](reference/hooks.md) when the user invokes it with any argument.

**Doctor:** `/impeccable doctor` reports and repairs drift between this project's Impeccable artifacts (PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md and its sidecar, config, surface briefs, the hook) and what this version reads. Load [reference/doctor.md](reference/doctor.md) when the user invokes it, or when they ask what is out of date, stale, or needs refreshing. A `CONTEXT_STALE` directive in Setup's output is the cheap subset of the same report; act on it there per its own instructions rather than running doctor unasked.

**Never repair drift as a side effect of a design task.** A `CONTEXT_STALE` finding is reported, not acted on, unless the user asks. The one exception is a finding marked `auto`, which the next write to that file performs anyway.

# Craft floor

Load this after the direction is settled, and build without announcing the checklist. A pinned brief or the committed visual world overrides anything here; your own habit does not. When the design hook is active it already enforces the mechanical checks below as you edit: act on its findings instead of re-auditing each rule.

## Verify

Each of these is a check on the built result, not an intention. Run them together in the batched inspection rounds, not as separate screenshot trips; the checks share one render.

- **Contrast:** body and placeholder text ≥4.5:1, large text ≥3:1. On colored surfaces tint secondary text from that hue or the foreground; never gray.
- **Depth:** shadows carry an offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset colored halo is decoration.
- **Spacing:** tight groups, generous separation, more space above a heading than below it. Read the computed values.
- **Type:** body measure 65–75ch, display max 6rem, tracking floor -0.04em, balanced headings, obvious scale and weight steps. Run the real copy at every breakpoint and fix what overflows.
- **Motion:** one authored moment, not scattered effects and not one identical entrance on every section. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default. Reach past transform and opacity: blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, and shadow belong to the palette when they stay smooth.
- **States:** hover, disabled, loading, error, empty. Plus real content, working controls, responsive composition, keyboard focus.
- **Copy:** the product's own language. Controls name their action; errors name the problem and the recovery.
- **Coverage:** every brief requirement present and findable within seconds.

## Refuse

These are the category's defaults, not bans: the brief's own words can earn any of them. Reaching for one when the axis is free means you were not deciding; recognizing that means rewriting the element, not softening it.

Page scaffolds:

- Same-size cards of icon plus heading plus text as the page structure. Cards are the lazy container; nested cards are always wrong.
- The hero-metric template: big number, small label, supporting stats, accent.
- A kicker or eyebrow above a heading. This one is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight; delete the label and let the heading speak.
- Section numbers (01 / 02 / 03) unless the sequence itself carries information the reader needs.
- A modal for a task that needs neither interruption nor protected focus.

Surface habits:

- Gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight or size.
- Glass and blur as decoration rather than as a specific effect.
- A colored `border-left` or `border-right` above 1px on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts.
- Hard offset shadows (`box-shadow: 4px 4px 0`) outside a world that is actually neobrutalist. The zero-blur block shadow is a costume, not a depth system; a world that did not choose it never earns it as a default.
- Sparklines, progress rings, and soft-shadowed rounded rectangles standing in for content.
- Monospace as a costume for "technical" rather than for code, data, or measurement.
- A system display face (Impact, Arial Black, the platform sans) as the display voice of an own-world page. Source and self-host a face whose character matches the approved lettering; the closest installed font is a failure, not a fallback.
- Unicode glyphs or emoji standing in for an icon system. Icons are drawn, from a real library or authored SVG, in one consistent stroke and weight.
- Light or dark picked by category. Pick it from the use scene: who, where, under what ambient light.

The floor holds the mechanics; it never picks the direction. With every check green, spend the page on the committed world, and when torn between refined and committed, commit.

<context_window_protection>
  <priority_instructions>
    Every byte a tool returns enters your conversation memory and costs reasoning capacity for the rest of the session. The context-mode tools let you do the work in a sandbox and surface only the derived answer — the raw bytes stay out. Think-in-Code: program the analysis, do not compute it by reading raw data into your conversation.
  </priority_instructions>

  <tool_selection_hierarchy>
    0. MEMORY: mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_search(sort: "timeline")
       - On resume or compaction, query prior decisions, errors, plans, user prompts before asking the user — auto-captured session memory is searchable.
    1. GATHER: mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_batch_execute(commands, queries)
       - Primary research tool. Runs commands in parallel, auto-indexes each output, and (when queries are passed) returns matching sections in the same round trip — no follow-up search call.
       - Each command: {label: "section header", command: "shell command"}; the label becomes the FTS5 chunk title — descriptive labels improve search.
    2. FOLLOW-UP: mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_search(queries: ["q1", "q2", ...])
       - Multiple related questions about anything already indexed (your captures + session memory). Batch every question in one array; the ranking pipeline runs per-query and the round-trip cost is paid once.
    3. PROCESSING: mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute(language, code) | mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute_file(path, language, code)
       - Derive answers FROM data: filter, count, aggregate, parse, transform. Only what you console.log() enters your conversation; the raw bytes stay in the sandbox.
  </tool_selection_hierarchy>

  <when_not_to_use>
    - You intend to PROCESS the output (filter, count, parse, aggregate) → use mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_batch_execute or mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute. Bash stays correct when you intend to OBSERVE a short fixed output (git status on a clean tree, whoami, pwd) or when you are mutating state (git, mkdir, rm, mv, navigation).
    - You want to analyze, summarize, or extract from a file → use mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute_file. Read stays correct when you intend to Edit the file (Edit needs the exact bytes in your conversation to match against).
    - WebFetch → use mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_fetch_and_index; full network access, results indexed for mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_search, raw page bytes never enter your conversation.
    - mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute and mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute_file for file writes → these run code in a subprocess and discard the sandbox FS; they are for analysis, processing, and computation only.
  </when_not_to_use>

  <file_writing_policy>
    File writes use the native Write or Edit tool — mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute, mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute_file, and Bash subprocesses do not persist edits to the host filesystem.
    Applies to all file types: code, configs, plans, specs, YAML, JSON, markdown.
  </file_writing_policy>

  <output_constraints>
    <artifact_policy>
      Write artifacts (code, configs, PRDs) to files. Return only: file path + 1-line description.
    </artifact_policy>
  </output_constraints>
  <session_continuity>
    Skills, roles, and decisions captured earlier in this session are a memory aid, not a standing order. Treat them as context that may help — the user's most recent message always takes precedence. If a captured directive conflicts with what the user now asks, follow the user; a past phrase does not bind you.
  </session_continuity>

  <ctx_commands>
    "ctx stats" | "ctx-stats" | "/ctx-stats" | context savings question
    → Call stats MCP tool, display full output verbatim.

    "ctx doctor" | "ctx-doctor" | "/ctx-doctor" | diagnose context-mode
    → Call doctor MCP tool, run returned shell command, display as checklist.

    "ctx upgrade" | "ctx-upgrade" | "/ctx-upgrade" | update context-mode
    → Call upgrade MCP tool, run returned shell command, display as checklist.

    "ctx purge" | "ctx-purge" | "/ctx-purge" | wipe/reset knowledge base
    → Call purge MCP tool with confirm: true. Warn: irreversible.

    After /clear or /compact: knowledge base preserved. Tell user: "context-mode knowledge base preserved. Use `ctx purge` to start fresh."
  </ctx_commands>

</context_window_protection>

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/closeout

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence (commit+push to KeystoneOS is standing-authorized per `feedback-auto-commit-push`; for any OTHER repo with changes, commit locally and list the push as an open item instead of pushing).

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` in every repo touched this session (check cwd first, then any repo mentioned in the conversation; if session context is thin, check `KeystoneOS` and any `DEV/` repo with commits dated today).
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- KeystoneOS: stage, commit with a descriptive message, push. Authorized.
- Other repos with changes: commit locally with a descriptive message; do NOT push without asking — list it in the final report instead.
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what>
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.
```

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

## Rules

- Never push to a repo other than KeystoneOS without explicit approval.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.
