# Handoff — Applied Performance status report system

**Written:** 2026-08-16
**Work done:** 2026-08-11 to 2026-08-12
**Status:** Built, verified, delivered. **Report #1 drafted but NOT SENT — its send date has passed.**

---

## What this was

Chris Ruf and Kenny Boyd asked Eric for a recurring status report — project statuses,
meetings, conversations, ideas, progress. Built via the `grilling` skill, then
implemented as a reusable skill plus template.

## The finding that shaped everything

**Eric had already specified this report himself.** It is **KR 4.1** in
`Projects/Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27.md` (v3):

> Friday report cadence live — biweekly email to Chris: Shipped / In Progress /
> Decisions Needed / Risks–No-Surprises / Next Two Weeks, <300 words. ≥3 sent by Aug 31.

It traces further back to a 2026-04-27 Chris Ruf check-in where Chris asked for recurring
meetings "to reduce anxiety" and to "increase visibility of ongoing projects." The August
ask was the third time. Everything was built to that existing spec rather than invented.

## Decisions made, with the reasoning

- **Purpose: alignment primary, defensibility secondary.** The real trigger is *credit* —
  Eric needs visible involvement with non-football/non-basketball sports. That is why the
  report carries sport tags and a coverage section; they are the point, not decoration.
- **Three layers, never merged.** Email (<300 words, what Chris reads) · PDF one-pager
  (attached, carries the detail the ceiling cut) · internal record (never sent, holds
  meetings/conversations/ideas/candid notes, and *is* the time documentation).
- **"Shipped" comes only from `output/_ledger.md`, never `portfolio.json` stage.** The
  registry marks `Sport_Tech_Vetting: shipped` while KR 1.2 shows Chris's sign-off
  outstanding. Telling a supervisor something shipped that he never approved is the one
  move that permanently damages the report's credibility.
- **Never depends on `weekly-review`.** That ritual lapsed 7 weeks earlier in the year and
  came back "after a 49-day silence" once before. A supervisor-facing report that inherits
  another ritual's failure rate is worse than none, because its absence is visible.
- **Read the v3 OKR doc only.** The cadence doc's KR table is the superseded v2 set of 9;
  `okr-tracker/SCOREBOARD.md` was generated 2026-06-12 against the retired 3-objective set
  and scores KRs that no longer exist. Both will produce wrong facts.
- **Cadence:** weekly through Aug 31 to clear the ≥3 target, then twice monthly (1st and
  3rd Friday). *1st-and-3rd-Friday was the assistant's pick, not Eric's — he said "twice a
  month, not every two weeks" then "every two weeks" a paragraph later. Still unconfirmed.*
- **Design: printed memorandum, not a dashboard.** Eric said v1 "looks AI-generated." He
  was right — status dots, badge rows, bolded stat lines, two-column grid. Rebuilt via the
  `impeccable` skill as a department memo in Charter, single column, one green hairline.
  The dashboard vocabulary is written into the template as an explicit anti-reference.
- **No Gmail drafting.** The connected Gmail is Eric's personal account, not Baylor. Drafts
  would land in the wrong mailbox. The skill emits paste-ready text; Eric sends from Outlook.

## Files created or modified

**The skill**
- `~/.claude/skills/status-report/SKILL.md` — the workflow
- `~/.claude/skills/status-report/assets/one-pager.html` — memo template (measure to 950px
  at 666px width before rendering; command is in SKILL.md Step 6)
- `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.json` — **fixed**: every path was still pointing at the
  old Windows machine (`C:\Users\eric_rash\...`). Added `okr_scoreboard`, `okr_tracker_dir`,
  `utilization_brief`, `canonical_projects`, `vault_status_reports`, `vault_output_ledger`.

**The vault**
- `~/SecondBrain/Templates/status-report.md` — three-layer template + all editorial rules
- `~/SecondBrain/Projects/Applied-Performance-Active-Projects.md` — canonical reportable
  project list; maps each project to a KR and a sport, names the 8 orphans honestly
- `~/SecondBrain/Inbox/status-reports/2026-08-14-email.txt` — report #1 email (267 words)
- `~/SecondBrain/Inbox/status-reports/2026-08-14-onepager.html` / `.pdf` — the memo
- `~/SecondBrain/Inbox/status-reports/2026-08-14-status.md` — internal record, `sent: false`

**Memory**
- `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory/project_status-report-sourcing.md`
- `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory/project_fireflies-cli-broken-on-mac.md`

## Next actions, most important first

1. **Send report #1 — or refresh it first.** It is dated 14 August; today is 16 August and
   it was never sent. Two facts in it have almost certainly gone stale: the framework
   presentation was "moved to Thursday, preparation underway" (Thursday 13 Aug has passed),
   and Noah's 15 Aug mentoring date has passed. **Verify both before sending.**
2. **The Aug 31 math is now tight.** KR 4.1 needs ≥3 *sent* by 31 August and zero are sent.
   From 16 August that means roughly 17, 24, and 31 August. There is no slack left.
3. **Confirm the cadence** — 1st-and-3rd Friday, or strict biweekly? Locks in by precedent
   after the second send.
4. **Unanswered offer:** log the five moved projects into `~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.json`
   (SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework, Sport_Tech_Vetting, Coach_Report,
   Transformative_Athlete_Experience, NCAA_BestPractices_Doc). 13 of 20 projects have zero
   update history, which starves the next report's auto-pull.
5. **Check Fireflies is auto-joining meetings.** It recorded nothing between 4 and 11 August,
   including the meeting that generated this whole requirement. If it keeps missing, every
   report runs thin and it reads as a productivity gap rather than a tooling gap.

## Mid-flight / open questions

- Was the Thursday 13 August framework presentation to John Allen and Micah delivered?
- Did Noah's mentoring cadence start, or is it still waiting on the school year?
- `vault_todo` and `pending_renames_file` in `_shared/config.json` point at files that do
  not exist. Harmless (created on demand by other skills) but worth knowing.

## How to run it

`/status-report` — pulls meetings, ledger, and project movement automatically, then asks a
short gap interview (target: under 5 minutes of Eric's time), then emits the three files
and runs a 20-point verification checklist. It does not send anything.

Saved and committed. Your email is now the reference the skill copies, not my draft.

**Four things it corrected:**

4. **The big one — my data sources were mostly looking at the wrong work.** Your report was Perch cameras, FirstBeat monitors, survey response rates, staff meetings, Linda. Almost none of that lives in your project registry or ledger. Those track what you *build*. You report what your *department runs*.

That means the auto-pull only covers about a third of a real report. The skill now says so plainly and puts equipment, installs, meetings, and stalled follow-ups at the top of the questions instead of the bottom.
